label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Sizwe, breathe, boet. Your engine isn’t necessarily finished, but **please take the key out and don’t crank it again**. Every time it turns, the pump is running on petrol without the lubrication it needs.

Kobus means well, but that’s old Land Rover advice. This is a modern common-rail diesel. **Don’t put diesel on top and don’t drive it**—the petrol is still in there.

Because it ran, stalled and was cranked again, damage to the pump and injectors is possible. It needs to be towed in and those checked first. If they’re OK, we’d drain the tank, flush the lines, fit a new fuel filter and bleed it. That’s usually around **R2 500 to R4 500**, but I can’t promise a total until we’ve inspected it. So don’t assume the R40k just yet.

Check your insurance policy before paying a tow guy cash—most policies have roadside towing. If you’re stuck somewhere unsafe, move yourself somewhere safe while you arrange it.

My shop is in Umbilo, open Saturday 7 to 12. Thabo, my guy, can drain it first thing once we’ve checked it. And borrow a bakkie for the sound and cake anyway—don’t plan your wedding around a drained tank!

If it helps, in my first year as an apprentice in 1995 I put diesel in the boss’s Golf. He still tells that story at every braai. You’re in good company.

Congrats on the wedding, laaitie. Now step away from that key.
